A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The original proof and experimental appendices can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, classification results, and SGD training curves in Tables 2–3 and Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds MNIST evaluation, a bias ablation, runtime measurements, and comparisons with other convex formulations in Tables 2–5.

M1.justification: v2 introduces and evaluates an optional first-layer bias variant, implemented by augmenting the inputs with a column of ones. The underlying CP formulation, SDP relaxation, and three-operator splitting rounding procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds a limited handwritten-digit classification setting using MNIST reduced to 20 PCA features. This extends the previous synthetic and tabular coverage to image-derived data while retaining all six existing datasets.

E2.justification: Appendix E adds a substantial comparison with closely related convex methods: Sahiner FW on Random regression and both Sahiner FW and Sahiner CP on Spiral classification (Tables 4–5). These methods were discussed but not evaluated in v1. The existing SGD, NNGP, and NTK comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce MNIST PCA preprocessing and an eight-million-iteration SGD budget, bias versus no-bias configurations, and runtime evaluation. The Sahiner comparisons specify 300 hidden neurons and set the FW epigraph parameter from SGD rather than bisection. Existing split rules, regularization values, rounding settings, and classification-threshold selection are retained.

E4.justification: The new SDP-NN-bias rows in Table 3 test the effect of adding first-layer biases across the classification datasets. The existing analyses of SGD width, regularization, and convergence, including the four Figure 2 plots, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 Random-dataset trials with standard deviations and selection of the best of five SGD initializations. Table 4 extends the existing averaging and standard-deviation practice to additional comparisons; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count is established.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands results with MNIST, bias variants, Sahiner comparisons, and runtimes. Existing kernel scores also change: Table 3 NNGP Iris F1 at gamma = 0.1 changes from 0.909 to 0.866, and NTK Pima F1 at gamma = 0.01 from 0.699 to 0.672. Shared SGD and SDP-NN classification entries and Table 2 loss/approximation-ratio values remain unchanged. The added finite-width comparator objectives do not establish performance gains over the SDP lower bounds.

T1.justification: Section 5 adds explicit asymptotic statements about interior-point arithmetic and iteration costs and O(n^3) storage for a CP factorization. The central equivalence theorems, critical-width bound, and appendix proofs are retained. Appendix A's explicit approximation-ratio inequality elaborates a lower-bound relationship already stated in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same principal claims: an exact finite-dimensional CP reformulation for sufficiently wide and infinite-width ReLU networks, a tractable SDP relaxation, and competitive classification performance. The revised conclusion emphasizes the existing data-dependent critical-width result without changing its scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands interpretation through discussion of generalization, optimization landscapes, and the distinctions between the exact formulation, NTK/NNGP, and finite-width SGD. Appendix E adds important qualifications about comparing Sahiner objectives with SDP lower bounds. Scalability limitations and the absence of rounding convergence guarantees were already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents MNIST preprocessing, its SGD learning rate of 10^-7 and eight-million-iteration budget, bias implementation, and solver runtimes. Appendix E identifies use of the Sahiner implementations and explains the FW parameter choice. Existing hardware, solver descriptions, other training settings, and the implementation-access statement remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands research positioning beyond the retained convex-training discussion. It adds comparisons with Fang et al. and connections to universal approximation, representer theorems, variation spaces, and capacity control, including Shenouda et al.'s quadratic width bound. Appendix A further connects the work to optimization-landscape, generalization, and factorization-rank research.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds a discussion appendix before the renumbered proofs, expands explanatory passages, rewrites the conclusion's emphasis, standardizes notation, and updates author, publication, and ethics text. This is localized editing and structural expansion rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively re-typeset in the ICLR format, changing the title and author block, headings, margins, and running headers. Tables 1–3 expand with dataset, method, and runtime fields, and Tables 4–5 are added. Both figures retain their underlying content but are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical context through evaluations of closely related convex methods, a bias ablation, limited MNIST coverage, and explicit computational costs. Expanded discussion clarifies the scope of the guarantees and the non-equivalence of compared objectives. These are useful incremental gains; the central proofs remain unchanged, while unexplained kernel-score revisions and mixed bias effects limit stronger conclusions.
